Dennis Schröder is a professional basketball player.
Dennis Schröder was born on 15 September 1993.
Dennis Schröder is German.
Dennis Schröder plays for the Brooklyn Nets of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Dennis Schröder previously played for SG Braunschweig and Phantoms Braunschweig in Germany.
Dennis Schröder spent his first five seasons in the NBA with the Atlanta Hawks.
Dennis Schröder also played two years with the Oklahoma City Thunder.
Dennis Schröder is the sole owner of his German hometown team, Basketball Loewen Braunschweig of the Basketball Bundesliga.
Dennis Schröder had been the majority shareholder of the team since 2018.
In 2023, Dennis Schröder led the German national team to their first World Cup title at the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup.
In 2023, Dennis Schröder was named the FIBA World Cup MVP.
On July 23, 2024, Dennis Schröder was chosen as a flag bearer for Paris 2024 alongside judoka Anna-Maria Wagner.
Dennis Schröder is the son of a German father and a Gambian mother.
Dennis Schröder has a brother and a younger sister.
Dennis Schröder found basketball at age 11 after being heavily involved with skateboarding until then.
Dennis Schröder chose to wear jersey number 17 in his honor, as it was his favorite number.
Dennis Schröder's father died in 2009.
Dennis Schröder's agent is Ademola Okulaja.
Schröder started playing professional basketball in 2010 for SG Braunschweig, farm team of Phantoms Braunschweig.
In his first season with SUM Baskets Braunschweig, Dennis Schröder averaged 7.8 points, 2.1 assists and 1.6 rebounds per game in a 2nd-tier German League.
In the 2011–12 season, Dennis Schröder made a breakthrough, averaging 17.8 points and 6.7 assists over 23 regular season games for SG Braunschweig.
Dennis Schröder's team went to the playoffs in the 2011–12 season where he averaged 18.8 points and 5.1 assists over 4 games.
In the same season, Dennis Schröder played 30 games for Phantoms Braunschweig of the German League, averaging 2.3 points, 0.7 assists and 0.8 rebounds in about 8 minutes per game.
In the 2012–13 season, Dennis Schröder played 32 games for Phantoms Braunschweig, averaging 12 points, 3.2 assists and 2.5 rebounds in 25 minutes per game.
For the 2012–13 season, Dennis Schröder was named the League's Most Improved Player as well as Best Young German Player.
In 2013, Dennis Schröder was announced to play at the 2013 Nike Hoop Summit for the World Select Team.
Before officially playing at the Nike Hoop Summit, Dennis Schröder decided to declare for the 2013 NBA draft.
On 27 June 2013, Dennis Schröder was selected by the Atlanta Hawks with the 17th overall pick in the 2013 NBA draft.
On 11 July 2013, Dennis Schröder signed with the Atlanta Hawks.
Dennis Schröder's minutes were cut due to frequent turnovers early in the season.
Shelvin Mack took over the second-string point guard position during this time.
Dennis Schröder spent time in the NBA Development League in December, with the Bakersfield Jam.
Dennis Schröder finished his rookie season playing in just 49 games for the Hawks, with 3.7 points in 13.1 minutes per game.
On 22 December 2014, Dennis Schröder scored a career-high 22 points in a 105–102 win over the Dallas Mavericks.
Dennis Schröder participated in the Rising Stars Challenge on 13 February 2015, recording 13 points, a game-high nine assists and three steals in Team World's 121–112 win over Team USA.
On 15 March 2015, Dennis Schröder had 24 points and 10 assists in a 91–86 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.
Dennis Schröder had a "breakout year" in 2014–15, increasing his averages to 10.0 points and 4.1 assists in 19.7 minutes per game, appearing in 77 regular season games with 10 starts.
Dennis Schröder continued to play behind All-Star Teague in 2015–16.
Dennis Schröder made just six starts in 80 games during the 2015–16 season.
During the 2015–16 season, Dennis Schröder averaged 11.0 points and 4.4 assists in 20.3 minutes per game.
Dennis Schröder shot 42% from the field and 32% from 3-point range during this time.
Defenders often dared him to shoot the three during his career with the Atlanta Hawks.
On 20 February 2016, Dennis Schröder recorded 25 points and 10 assists in a 117–109 overtime loss to the Milwaukee Bucks.
In Game 1 of the Hawks' second round playoff series against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Dennis Schröder scored a playoff career-high 27 points in a 104–93 loss.
On 26 October 2016, Dennis Schröder signed a four-year, $70 million contract extension with the Atlanta Hawks.
Dennis Schröder took the reins as the Hawks' lead guard in 2016–17 following Teague's trade to the Indiana Pacers.
On 8 November 2016, Dennis Schröder scored a then career-high 28 points in a 110–106 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On 30 November 2016, Dennis Schröder scored 14 of his career-high 31 points in the fourth quarter of the Hawks' 109–107 loss to the Phoenix Suns.
On 9 December 2016, Dennis Schröder set a new career high with 33 points in a 114–110 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.
In Game 5 of the Hawks' first round playoff series against the Washington Wizards, Dennis Schröder led the Hawks with 29 points, making a career high-tying five 3s, and 11 assists in a 103–99 loss.
On 25 July 2018, Dennis Schröder was traded to the Oklahoma City Thunder in a three-team deal involving the Hawks and the Philadelphia 76ers.
In his first season with the Thunder, Dennis Schröder was positioned as the team's sixth man, coming off the bench behind Russell Westbrook.
On 16 October, Dennis Schröder recorded 21 points, eight rebounds, six assists and three steals in a 108–100 loss to the Golden State Warriors during his debut for the Thunder.
On 7 November, Dennis Schröder scored a then season-high 28 points in a 95–86 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On 21 November, Dennis Schröder scored a season-high 32 points off the bench in a 123–95 win over the Warriors.
On 1 February 2019, Dennis Schröder scored 24 of his 28 points in the second quarter of the Thunder's 118–102 win over the Miami Heat.
On 3 March, Dennis Schröder recorded 17 points and a career-high 11 rebounds in a 99–95 win over the Memphis Grizzlies.
Dennis Schröder led the league in scoring off the bench with 18.9 points per game during his second season with the Thunder.
During this time, Dennis Schröder shot a career-high 46.9% from the field and 38.5% on 3-point field goals.
Dennis Schröder finished as the runner-up to Montrezl Harrell in voting for the NBA Sixth Man of the Year.
On 18 November 2020, Dennis Schröder was traded to the Los Angeles Lakers in exchange for Danny Green and the draft rights to first-round pick Jaden McDaniels.
Dennis Schröder made his Lakers debut on 22 December 2020, putting up 14 points, 12 rebounds, and eight assists in a 116–109 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers.
During the season, Dennis Schröder was sidelined twice due to league's COVID-19 health protocols.
Dennis Schröder started 61 games during the regular season for the Lakers, averaging 15.4 points and 5.8 assists per game.
His shooting percentages were 43.7% from the field and 33.5% on 3-pointers.
In the playoffs, Dennis Schröder's numbers dropped to 14.3 points and 2.8 assists while shooting 40.3% from the field and 31.9% from three-point range.
The Lakers were eliminated in six games by Phoenix.
On 13 August 2021, Dennis Schröder signed with the Boston Celtics on a one-year, $5.9 million taxpayer mid-level exception contract.
Dennis Schröder chose to wear number 71 with the Celtics as his usual number 17 had been retired by the Celtics in honor of John Havlicek.
Dennis Schröder became only the fourth known player in the history of the league to wear the number 71 and the first since McCoy McLemore in 1965.
On 10 February 2022, Dennis Schröder was traded, along with Enes Freedom and Bruno Fernando, to the Houston Rockets in exchange for Daniel Theis.
Dennis Schröder was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a shoulder injury on 29 March.
On 16 September 2022, Dennis Schröder signed with the Los Angeles Lakers again to a one-year, $2.64 million deal.
Schröder chose the Lakers over the Toronto Raptors and Phoenix Suns citing "unfinished business" with the Lakers.

During his first practice on his second stint with the team, Dennis Schröder claimed that the Lakers never offered him a four-year, $84 million contract extension during the previous free agency before the start of the 2021–22 NBA season.
On 4 January 2023, Dennis Schröder scored 14 of his season-high 32 points in the fourth quarter to lead the Lakers to a 112–109 win over the Miami Heat.
On 20 January 2023, Dennis Schröder put up 19 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, and made a game-winning layup in a 122–121 win over the Memphis Grizzlies.
During their hard-fought play-in game on 11 April 2023 against the Minnesota Timberwolves, Dennis Schröder scored 21 points on 41.7% field goal shooting.

Dennis Schröder made three out of four three-pointers in this game including a clutch tiebreaking corner three-point shot off a kick out pass from LeBron James with 1.4 seconds remaining in the regulation.
The Lakers were up by three at that point, but eventually lost to Minnesota's veteran point guard Mike Conley Jr.'s game-tying corner three-point attempt with 0.1 seconds left.
On 30 June 2023, Dennis Schröder signed a two-year, $26 million contract with the Toronto Raptors.
The deal took up Toronto's entire mid-level exception allowing the organization about $8.7 million below the luxury tax threshold.
Dennis Schröder was Schröder's sixth team as he entered his tenth season in the NBA.
On 25 October 2023, Dennis Schröder made his Raptors debut, putting up 22 points and seven assists in a 97–94 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves.
On 13 December 2023, after a 135-128 win against the Atlanta Hawks, Dennis Schröder achieved 10,000 career points.
On 8 February 2024, Dennis Schröder was traded alongside Thaddeus Young to the Brooklyn Nets in exchange for Spencer Dinwiddie.
Dennis Schröder made his Nets debut on 10 February, putting up 15 points and 12 assists in a 123–103 win over the San Antonio Spurs.
Dennis Schröder has been a member of the German national under-18 and German national under-20 teams.
Dennis Schröder played in the 2012 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship, helping Germany to fifth place with averages of 6.1 points, 2 assists, and 1.8 rebounds in 14.6 minutes on the court.
On 27 July 2014, Dennis Schröder made his debut for the senior Germany national basketball team against Finland.
Dennis Schröder played at EuroBasket 2015, where Germany did not qualify for the knock-out stage and finished in 18th place.
Dennis Schröder returned to EuroBasket 2017, leading Germany to the quarterfinals with averages of 23.7 points and 5.6 assists per game.
In 2020, Dennis Schröder expressed a desire to play for Germany at the 2020 Summer Olympics.
However, the German Basketball Federation was unable to meet the financial insurance requirements for his participation in the 2020 Summer Olympics.
Dennis Schröder returned to EuroBasket 2022 and led Germany to third place, being named to the EuroBasket All-Tournament Team.
During this run, Dennis Schröder had a famous win over Greece with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the roster.
Schröder averaged team-highs 22.1 points and 7.1 assists per game during EuroBasket 2022.
Dennis Schröder led the German national team to their first World Cup title at the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup.
The team went undefeated, defeating top-ranked teams such as Australia and the United States.
After the final between Germany and Serbia, Dennis Schröder was named FIBA World Cup MVP with averages of 17.9 points and 6.7 assists per game.
At the 2024 Paris Olympics, Dennis Schröder's German national team lost to France in the semi-finals.
The team then lost to Serbia in the bronze medal game, finishing without a medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics.
Dennis Schröder is married and has three children.
Dennis Schröder adopted his "signature" patch of bleached blonde hair upon leaving Germany for the United States as suggested by his mother.
Dennis Schröder is a devout Muslim who prays before games and before going to sleep.
Dennis Schröder is a teetotaler and has never consumed alcohol in his life.
In May 2021, Dennis Schröder said he was the only Lakers player who had not been vaccinated against COVID-19.
After the Nets were eliminated from the 2024 playoffs, Dennis Schröder joined FC Germania Bleckenstedt soccer team of the German Landesliga Braunschweig.
